Subject: Baseline IO rates & model compatibility — initial ask

Hi Ben,

We are kicking off an internal evaluation of hosted inference providers and want a quick baseline for per-1M token pricing (separate input vs output rates) and a list of supported/certified models for the hosted API. High-level context:
- Novacare is building a patient triage assistant (text-in + long-form summaries).
- Expected steady-state: ~15M tokens/month initially; peak bursts up to 80M.
- Latency target: sub-300ms for short-chat turn (prefers lower-latency variants if you have them).

Can you send: 1) standard per-1M token input/output rates for your hosted tiers (no commitment), 2) a short list of recommended models for this workload (incl. rough relative cost tiers), and 3) whether you offer standard volume-break discounts or 12-month commit pricing?

Attaching our 6-month traffic projection to help with modeling.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call later this week.

Best,

Ben — thanks, quick answers below (pasted under your questions):

> Is the 15M tokens/month a steady average or the total across environments (prod + staging)?
It9s total customer-facing production traffic (we9ll keep a small staging footprint in a different account).

> Will you need HIPAA / PHI safeguards or SOC2-level audit evidence for the pilot?
Yes, HIPAA is a hard requirement. We also need the vendor to provide SOC2 Type II reports and evidence of KMS integration for keys. If you have a private/VPC path for pilot customers, please note compatibility.

> Are you more sensitive to per-token cost or latency?

On discounts: procurement asked if there's 10-15% off standard rates for a 12-month committed volume (we can commit to 180M tokens over 12 months if the economics work).

Let me know if you9d like a recorded call.

Samira — appreciate the details. Below is a concise baseline for hosted (no-commit) pricing and a recommended model roster for a HIPAA-sensitive, low-latency triage flow. This is intended as a starting point — we can provide formal pricing and an MSA via DocuSign once you confirm interest.

1) Baseline per-1M token IO rates (hosted API, US region, list price, USD):
- Redwood-compact-8B (low-latency family): Input $2.50 / 1M tokens | Output $4.75 / 1M tokens
- Redwood-standard-30B: Input $6.25 / 1M tokens | Output $11.20 / 1M tokens
- Redwood-rlhf-70B (high-quality): Input $12.00 / 1M tokens | Output $21.50 / 1M tokens
- Quantized open-fallback (gptj-6B-quant): Input $1.10 / 1M tokens | Output $2.00 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- Input = tokens consumed by prompts, system messages, embeddings; Output = tokens generated by model.
- Listed prices reflect our hosted standard tier (no upfront commit).
- We can recommend Redwood-compact-8B for your latency target (~sub-300ms P50, ~<450ms P95 under steady load) and Redwood-standard-30B for cases where quality matters more than micro-latency.

2) Compliance & deployment notes:
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA workflows on Dedicated + Private deployments. For hosted pilots requiring PHI, we can offer a guarded path (BAA + restricted hosting configurations); Laura will follow up with SOC2/BAA paperwork.
- Key management: KMS integrations available; we can discuss HSM options for Private.

3) Discounts & commitment path:
- Volume discounts: standard breakpoints at 100M and 500M tokens / month. For a 12-month commit (180M total), we typically offer a 10% discounted list rate across the committed volume; additional discounts can be structured for multi-year or higher-volume commitments.
- We can also propose a blended committed price if you want to mix compact + standard usage (helps manage cost while meeting latency).

4) Next steps and attachments:
- Attached: redwood-ratecard-v1.pdf (compact summary) and I9ve run a preliminary cost model against your CSV — Laura will circulate the exported spreadsheet with line-item math.
- Proposed next step: 30-min technical + procurement sync to cover HIPAA path and demo of the compact-8B latency profile. Please share 2 windows that work and we9ll lock something in.

Happy to refine.
